title: Session Hotspot Indexing & Sampling Policy — Notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal sketch for a lightweight per-session "hotspot index" that drives adaptive prefetch and eviction decisions.
- Goal: identify recurring token prefixes / context slices that are high-value for fast re-use, without holding full session state in memory for all sessions.

Problem statement:
- Many sessions have a small set of recurring prompts or context fragments that get reused across turns (system messages, user templates, recent referenced docs).
- We want to capture just the "hotspots" (small fingerprints + access frequency) to:
  * prefetch KV cache entries proactively when a session is active,
  * prefer eviction of cold shards,
  * inform sampling/QA for micro-evals (are we losing quality when we evict hot entries?).

Design constraints / requirements:
- Extra per-session metadata must be tiny (<< 1KB).
- Index updates should be append-only-ish and lock-free across fast paths.
- Compatible with multi-host session migration and snapshot/offload.
- Can be persisted to per-tenant on-disk store or central fast KV (redis/rocks).
- Privacy: no storing raw PII; only hashed fingerprints + small metadata.

API surface (sketch, JSON-over-HTTP):
- GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/hotspots\  returns current hotspot index summary (no PII).
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/hotspots/update\  body: {updates: [ {fingerprint, delta_score, tag}] }\  used by runtime fast-path to bump weights asynchronously.
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/hotspots/commit-snapshot\  pushes a compact snapshot when evicting or snapshotting session.
- DELETE /v1/sessions/{session_id}/hotspots\  clear index on explicit user request (GDPR).

Example response (GET):
{
  "session_id": "s_abc123",
  "last_updated": "2025-02-18T13:07:22Z",
  "hotspots": [
    {"fingerprint":"f1e2...","score":"12.4","tag":"system_prompt_v2","approx_len":"32"},
    {"fingerprint":"aa09...","score":"4.1","tag":"user_template_invoice","approx_len":"48"}
  ],
  "prefetch_guidance": {"budget_tokens": "512","priority": ["f1e2...","aa09..."]}
}

Index representation (in-memory compact):
- Fixed-size slot array (e.g., 16 slots) per session; open addressing.
- Each slot stores: 8B fingerprint (SipHash truncated) + 2B score (fp16-ish quantized) + 1B tag_id + 1B ttl/decay_counter => ~12B per slot => 192B per-session for 16 slots.
- Eviction: decay by time windows + occasional reservoir sampling to surface spikes.

Config schema (YAML-ish sketch for runtime / console):
- hotspot.index_slots: 16
- hotspot.decay_alpha: 0.85   # multiplicative decay per minute window
- hotspot.bump_amount: 1.0   # amount added on detection
- hotspot.prefetch_budget_tokens: 512
- hotspot.prefetch_trigger_threshold: 5.0  # score threshold to prefetch
- hotspot.max_prefetch_items: 4
- hotspot.persistence_mode: "per-tenant-redis" | "local-ssdsnap"

Update path pseudocode (fast-path, non-blocking):
1) on serving runtime seeing a repeated prefix X:
   fp = truncate_hash(X)
   idx = fp % slots_len
   do CAS into slot: if slot.fp==fp -> slot.score += bump_amount; else if slot.empty -> insert(fp, bump_amount, tag); else linear_probe
2) fire async write to hot-update queue that coalesces per-session and flushes to persistence every 5s or when score crosses commit threshold.

Sampling / Prefetch policy (sketch):
- After each request, compute top-K hotspots where score >= prefetch_trigger_threshold.
- Prefetch budget = min(prefetch_budget_tokens, per-request-token-limit).
- Choose top items by score until budget exhausted or max_prefetch_items reached.
- Prefetch operation = async fetch KV cache for (session_id, fingerprint) and attach to KV warmup pool.

Lightweight telemetry to monitor efficacy:
- metrics: hotspot.prefetch.hits, hotspot.prefetch.misses, hotspot.prefetch_latency_ms, hotspot.evicted_hot_count, hotspot.size_distribution
- sampling: capture small sample of requests where prefetches triggered + whether a later token stream used prefetched entries (label true/false).
- retention: keep sample traces for 7 days.

ASCII dataflow diagram:

Client -> Edge Proxy -> Serving Runtime -> Prefetch Worker -> KV Store
                 |               ^
                 |               | (async guidance)
                 +-> Hotspot index update queue (append-only)

Notes / heuristics (brain dump):
- Tagging: tag_id helps classify hotspots (system, user_template, doc_ref). We can map id->string in tenant metadata to keep per-slot size small.
- Use fp16-ish score to minimize per-slot memory but store high-res values in persistent snapshots.
- When migrating session to another host, include snapshot commit with top-N hotspots; receiving host merges shallowly to avoid spikes.
- Cold-start recovery: on new host, prefetch top-1 hotspot only until warm-up completes.

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to detect adversarial input that forces many unique fingerprints? -> cap per-request bump rate + incremental decay.
- Should we persist tags or only in-memory? Persisted tags useful for offline analysis but increase storage.
- How will this interact with quantized KV caches where keys are shard-specific? Need stable mapping.

Migration checklist (for prototype -> alpha):
- [ ] Implement in-serving fast-path CAS-based slot ops (C++).
- [ ] Background coalescer that batches writes to Redis or ssd snap files.
- [ ] Prefetch worker + integration test with kv-cache mock.
- [ ] Telemetry events & dashboards (prefetch hit/miss).
- [ ] Privacy review + GDPR delete hook.

Experiments to run:
- Compare tail latency and token cost for sessions with hotspot-index prefetch vs baseline.
- A/B: prefetch budget 256 vs 512 vs 1024 tokens.
- Quality regression: measure token-level perplexity change when hotspots are evicted.

References / links to related tickets / notes:
- CONFLUENCE-1234: previous notes on "micro-cache warmup"
- JIRA-RT-7890: prototype task for session snapshot format
- slack:#serving-runtime thread: "prefetch experiments feb 2025"

Quick TODOs for next sync:
- Decide persistence backing (redis vs per-tenant ssd). (Ben)
- Sketch proto wire-format for hotspot snapshot (Ishaan)
- Add privacy-preserving fingerprinting doc + approval path (ask Legal). (me)

Rough timeline idea:
- 2w: get fast-path insert/decay in local dev + unit tests
- 4w: background writer + prefetch worker integration tests + perf harness
- 8w: small closed-alpha with 5 internal customers, telemetry review

Random notes to self:
- Keep slot_count power-of-two to simplify modulo ops.
- Consider probabilistic counting (CMS) if we need histogram aggregation across hosts.
- Might derive hotspot tags from normalized prompt heuristics (strip uuids, timestamps) to improve collisions.

End of notebook.

-- maya
